articles.title: Parchment
articles.summary: Flat even satin grey with a faint paper-like grain, no flake, no shine, like old parchment. Takes your colour: a plain solid paint with a soft low-sheen, slightly aged satin finish and no sparkle, like dry old lacquer.
articles.what: Up close: The paint render is a flat uniform grey panel with no grain, flake or pattern, so up close there is nothing visible; the look is in the shine numbers only: low metal (about 50), medium-high roughness (110) and a dull clearcoat (140). The stretched strip is only contrast-boosted noise, real. From a distance: Takes your colour: a plain solid paint with a soft low-sheen, slightly aged satin finish and no sparkle, like dry old lacquer. Measured spec (average): metal 50, roughness 110, coat 140. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, show car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Parchment on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: even finish on all panels
Best as a calm base under graphics or distressing
Numbers read cleanly in any contrasting colour on the smooth, even surface.
Fine grain or dust: adds the weathered paper feel the base lacks
Pairs well with: brown leather, brass, cream, dark wood.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a different look from Old School in the picture: both renders are the same flat grey; only the shine differs, Parchment is duller and less metallic
Not paper-textured: card says paper-like grain, the render has none
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to high gloss finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 50 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 110 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 140 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to high gloss finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine grain or dust: adds the weathered paper feel the base lacks; distressed fade or wear: leans into the vintage look
Patterns to avoid: glitter or flake patterns: wrong mood for a dull vintage finish
Spec overlays that work: subtle micro grain: aged surface feel; gloss band stripes: contrast against the dull base
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Patinated Bronze
articles.summary: Fine, dense speckled texture in warm bronze and green tones, like aged metal. Reads as a muted bronze-olive car with a faint diagonal twill; green flecks give an aged copper tint and the stripes disappear.
articles.what: Up close: Bronze-brown ground peppered with tiny orange-rust and sea-green dots, 2-3 px each, lined up in fine diagonal rows like denim twill, about 8 px between rows. Green and orange stay balanced, so it looks like verdigris in the weave of copper. From a distance: Reads as a muted bronze-olive car with a faint diagonal twill; green flecks give an aged copper tint and the stripes disappear. Measured spec (average): metal 181, roughness 114, coat 90. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, trim, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Patinated Bronze" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, doors, roof: even all-over texture
Trim and bumpers: tiny flecks still read as aged metal
Cream or black numbers with an outline read fine; green or brown numbers disappear into the flecks.
Wear or scratch overlay: heightens the aged look
Pairs well with: black, brown, cream, chrome.
pitfalls: Not denim fabric: it is metallic with sparkle, in bronze and green
Not a smooth bronze metal: tiny dots and diagonal rows are the texture
Avoid: bright colours, matte finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 181 (true metallic), roughness 114 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 90 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: bright colours, matte finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: wear or scratch overlay: heightens the aged look; dust or grime fade at edges: more patina
Patterns to avoid: carbon fibre or twill: doubles the diagonal and moires; bright neon patterns: wrong mood
Spec overlays that work: gloss band: crisp stripe through the satin; micro grain: not needed, already fine
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
